title: The Team's runner and daily audit, on staging only (Piece 2, P2-3 and P2-4)
why: Jason's Piece 2 (decisions/0179; handoffs/piece2-team.md §5, approved 2026-11-25, Q1 A and Q4 B): a scheduled job that, on the staging copy only and while its switch is on, takes one ticket and does one step for one working role, logs it with Undo, and stops. The Work queue's tables become records, so live's tasks reach staging by catch-up and what the agents do reaches live only at Publish, in the approved batch. Nothing runs on live. Jason, 2026-11-25: "limit agents and build to only the initial work que stage until I fully vet the builds" and "The team decision tree is what I need to approve for agents to begin assuming full capacity": Agents work up to Planning by default (the Project Manager proposes its gate, a person's Accept moves it; the Architect's hand-off off), raised only by the Founder one stage at a time once the decision tree, drawn from the runner's constants and tied to their fingerprint, is approved; a rule change clears the approval and lowers it to Planning. Agents never take a ticket: a person's Give it to the Team assigns it. The queue says what agents found and suggested. With it, P2-4: Jason's Piece 2 (decisions/0179; handoffs/piece2-team.md §6, approved 2026-11-25): once a day on staging the Operations & Reconciliation Manager reads Site health's findings, late or failed jobs and open alarms, opens one Audit ticket per new finding, and a day later confirms it (opening a Work ticket, or a Resolution for a Tier 3) or clears it as noise. Nothing runs on live. Tier 3 is found by what a finding touches (decisions/0179's note, 2026-11-25): a page, file, job, service, library or table in TeamRunner::TIER3_AREAS, each taken from the live code. Words alone never make Tier 3: they leave it Tier 2 with a flag, "Words suggest a Tier 3 boundary: a person checks", which a person settles on the ticket (It's Tier 2, or It's Tier 3, which opens its Resolution), kept in the History.
